item.text: {"summary":"Propagate the supplied time zone through time formatting and parsing.","explanation":"The formatting failures share one cause: FormatTime(format, t, tz) passes UTC to CCTZ instead of tz. In Time.TimeZoneAt, formatting nov01_ci.pre and the DST transition values in nyc therefore shows UTC fields and offsets instead of the asserted New York civil times. The same mismatch appears in Time.FromTM for t formatted with nyc, and at the extreme instants in Time.ConversionSaturation when formatting with plus14 and minus12. ParseTime has the parallel issue: for the no-offset input \"2013-06-28 19:08:09\" with the Los Angeles zone, the test expects ci.cs to be 2013-06-28T19:08:09 but observes 2013-06-28T12:08:09, consistent with interpreting the fields as UTC. Passing tz to CCTZ restores the requested zone; CCTZ parsing continues to honor an explicit UTC offset in the input.","edits":[{"path":"absl/time/format.cc","old":"return cctz::detail::format(std::string(format), parts.sec, parts.fem,\n                              cctz::time_zone(absl::UTCTimeZone()));","new":"return cctz::detail::format(std::string(format), parts.sec, parts.fem,\n                              cctz::time_zone(tz));"},{"path":"absl/time/format.cc","old":"cctz::time_zone(absl::UTCTimeZone()), &parts.sec, &parts.fem, &error);","new":"cctz::time_zone(tz), &parts.sec, &parts.fem, &error);"}]}
